q: In the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz, what color are the magic slippers Dorothy wears?
note: They were silver in L. Frank Baum's novel, and MGM switched them to ruby to show off Technicolor.

q: In the 1977 film Star Wars, what is the name of Han Solo's battered freighter?
note: Han brags that it made the Kessel Run in less than twelve parsecs, a boast about distance rather than time.

q: In the 1960 thriller Psycho, where in the Bates Motel is Marion Crane murdered?
note: Bernard Herrmann scored the entire film for string instruments alone, including those shrieking violins.

q: In the 1985 film Back to the Future, what make of car does Doc Brown turn into a time machine?
note: The car has to hit 88 miles per hour and draw 1.21 gigawatts of power to jump through time.

q: What is the dying word spoken in the opening scene of the 1941 film Citizen Kane?
note: Orson Welles co-wrote, directed and starred in the picture, his first feature film.

q: Which actress played the singing governess Maria in the 1965 film The Sound of Music?
note: She won the Best Actress Oscar for Mary Poppins, released the year before.

q: In the 1975 film Jaws, what is the name of the beach town terrorized by the great white shark?
note: The mechanical shark broke down so often that the director kept it hidden, which only made the film scarier.

q: Which actor played the aging Don Vito Corleone in the 1972 film The Godfather?
note: He won Best Actor for the role and refused the award in protest at Hollywood's portrayal of Native Americans.

q: What is the name of the ship's computer that turns on the crew in the 1968 film 2001: A Space Odyssey?
note: Each letter of HAL sits one place before IBM in the alphabet, which Arthur C. Clarke always insisted was a coincidence.

q: In the 1982 film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, what brand of candy does Elliott use to coax E.T. into his house?
note: Mars turned down the chance to use M&M's, and sales of Reese's Pieces soared after the film opened.

q: In the 1939 epic Gone with the Wind, what is the name of Scarlett O'Hara's family plantation?
note: Hattie McDaniel won Best Supporting Actress for the film, the first Academy Award given to a Black performer.

q: What is the name of the snowbound Colorado hotel in the 1980 film The Shining?
note: Stephen King disliked Kubrick's version so much that he backed a more faithful television remake in 1997.

q: Which heavyweight champion does Rocky Balboa fight in the climax of the 1976 film Rocky?
note: Sylvester Stallone wrote the screenplay himself and refused to sell it unless he could star in it.

q: Which 1979 science fiction film introduced Sigourney Weaver as Warrant Officer Ripley?
note: Ridley Scott kept the cast in the dark about the chestburster scene, so much of their horror is genuine.

q: What is the name of the nightclub run by Humphrey Bogart's character in the 1942 film Casablanca?
note: The film's most quoted line, 'Play it again, Sam,' is never actually spoken in it.

q: Which star sings and dances the title number through a downpour in the 1952 musical Singin' in the Rain?
note: The story is set during Hollywood's chaotic switch from silent pictures to talkies.

q: Which actor played T. E. Lawrence in the 1962 epic Lawrence of Arabia?
note: He was nominated for eight acting Oscars across his career and never won a competitive one.

q: How many different roles did Peter Sellers play in the 1964 satire Dr. Strangelove?
note: He was meant to play a fourth, the bomber pilot, but an injury handed that part to Slim Pickens.

q: Which 1974 Roman Polanski film about Los Angeles water rights ends with the line 'Forget it, Jake. It's Chinatown'?
note: Screenwriter Robert Towne took home the film's only Academy Award.

q: Which 1959 Billy Wilder comedy closes with the line 'Nobody's perfect'?
note: Joe E. Brown delivers it after learning that his fiancée is a man in disguise.

q: Which actor played the penniless artist Jack Dawson in the 1997 film Titanic?
note: The film won eleven Academy Awards, tying the record set by the 1959 epic Ben-Hur.

q: In the 1999 film The Matrix, what color pill does Neo swallow to learn the truth?
note: Its slow-motion 'bullet time' shots were made with a ring of still cameras firing in sequence.

q: In the 1994 film Forrest Gump, Forrest says that life is like a box of what?
note: Tom Hanks won Best Actor for the role, his second win in a row after Philadelphia.

q: In the 1990 comedy Home Alone, what is the first name of the boy left behind when his family flies to Paris?
note: John Hughes wrote the screenplay after wondering what might happen if he forgot one of his own children on a trip.

q: In the 2001 film Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone, what is the name of the school Harry is invited to attend?
accept: Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
note: Outside North America the same film was released as Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone.

q: Which actor played the Joker in the 2008 film The Dark Knight?
note: He died before the film opened and won a posthumous Oscar for Best Supporting Actor.

q: In the 1993 film Jurassic Park, what is the name of the island where the dinosaur park is built?
note: Michael Crichton wrote the 1990 novel and then co-wrote the screenplay.

q: Who wrote and directed the 1994 crime film Pulp Fiction?
note: It won the Palme d'Or at Cannes and the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay.

q: In the 1994 film The Shawshank Redemption, what does Andy Dufresne hang on his cell wall to hide his escape tunnel?
note: The film barely made its money back in cinemas and became a favorite only through television reruns and video.

q: Which actor played Hannibal Lecter in the 1991 film The Silence of the Lambs?
note: The film swept the top five Oscars, something only two other films have ever managed.

q: The opening sequence of the 1998 film Saving Private Ryan re-creates the D-Day landing on which Normandy beach?
note: The landing was actually filmed on a stretch of Irish coast in County Wexford.

q: Which actor played the Roman general Maximus in the 2000 film Gladiator?
note: The film took Best Picture and Crowe took Best Actor.

q: In the 2001 film The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring, which hobbit is given the task of carrying the One Ring?
note: Peter Jackson shot all three installments back to back in New Zealand.

q: On which lush alien moon is the 2009 film Avatar set?
note: Pandora is a moon orbiting a gas giant, not a planet in its own right.

q: What is the name of the hidden African nation ruled by T'Challa in the 2018 film Black Panther?
note: It became the first superhero film ever nominated for the Best Picture Oscar.

q: Which 2016 musical was mistakenly announced as the Best Picture winner before Moonlight was named the real winner?
note: The presenters had been handed a duplicate Best Actress envelope, which Emma Stone had just won for that same film.

q: In Steven Spielberg's otherwise black-and-white 1993 film Schindler's List, what color is the coat worn by a small girl in the ghetto?
note: The film won Spielberg his first Academy Award for Best Director.

q: Which pair of filmmaking brothers wrote and directed the 2007 Best Picture winner No Country for Old Men?
note: Javier Bardem won Best Supporting Actor as the coin-flipping killer Anton Chigurh.

q: Which 2000 Christopher Nolan thriller tells the story of a man with no short-term memory largely in reverse order?
note: It grew out of a short story written by the director's brother, Jonathan Nolan.

q: Which comedian wrote and directed the 2017 horror film Get Out, winning an Oscar for its screenplay?
note: He was already well known for the sketch series Key & Peele.

q: In the sitcom Friends, which premiered in 1994, what is the name of the coffee house where the group hangs out?
note: The six leads eventually negotiated their salaries as a single group rather than individually.

q: In The Simpsons, which began as a half-hour series in 1989, what is the name of the town where the family lives?
note: The show has never settled which state it is in, and the vagueness is the joke.

q: In the series Breaking Bad, which began in 2008, what subject did Walter White teach in high school?
note: He takes the alias Heisenberg, borrowed from the German physicist.

q: On Sesame Street, which first aired in 1969, which grouchy character lives in a trash can?
note: Caroll Spinney performed both Oscar and Big Bird for nearly fifty years.

q: The series M*A*S*H, which ran from 1972 to 1983, is set during which war?
note: The show lasted eleven years, more than three times as long as the war it depicted.

q: In the American version of The Office, which premiered in 2005, what is the name of the paper company where the staff work?
note: The branch sits in Scranton, Pennsylvania, and the series was adapted from Ricky Gervais's British original.

q: What is the rarely used first name of Kramer, the neighbor on the sitcom Seinfeld, which ran from 1989 to 1998?
note: The character was based on Kenny Kramer, a real-life neighbor of co-creator Larry David.

q: In the HBO series Game of Thrones, which premiered in 2011, what three words serve as the motto of House Stark?
note: The series was adapted from George R. R. Martin's novels, starting with A Game of Thrones.

q: What is the name of the starship commanded by Captain Kirk in the original Star Trek series, which debuted in 1966?
note: The original series was canceled after three seasons and only became a phenomenon in reruns.

q: In which American city is the bar in the sitcom Cheers, which ran from 1982 to 1993?
note: The exterior shots show a real pub then known as the Bull & Finch.

q: Which comedian starred as Lucy Ricardo in the 1950s sitcom I Love Lucy?
note: It was shot on film with three cameras before a live audience, which is why the reruns still look sharp.

q: What is the surname of the skeptical medical doctor partnered with Fox Mulder in The X-Files, which began in 1993?
note: Gillian Anderson was a near-unknown, and the network had to be talked into casting her.

q: Which actor played mob boss Tony Soprano in the HBO drama that began in 1999?
note: The series ends mid-scene with an abrupt cut to black that still divides viewers.

q: What was the nickname of Henry Winkler's leather-jacketed character on the 1970s sitcom Happy Days?
note: A 1977 episode in which he water-skis over a shark gave the world the phrase 'jumping the shark.'

q: In which city do the four housemates live in the sitcom The Golden Girls, which premiered in 1985?
note: All four leads won an Emmy for the series, a rare clean sweep.

q: What is the name of the dark parallel world in the series Stranger Things, which premiered in 2016?
note: The show is set in the fictional town of Hawkins, Indiana, during the 1980s.

q: The 1980 cliffhanger 'Who shot J.R.?' left the world guessing about a character on which prime-time soap opera?
note: The culprit turned out to be Kristin, his scheming sister-in-law.

q: Which writer created, hosted and narrated the anthology series The Twilight Zone, which debuted in 1959?
note: He wrote a large share of the episodes himself, often smuggling social commentary past the censors.

q: Which actor played the loud-mouthed bigot Archie Bunker on the 1970s sitcom All in the Family?
note: The series was adapted from the British sitcom Till Death Us Do Part.

q: What is the name of the New York advertising agency where Don Draper works in the early seasons of Mad Men, which premiered in 2007?
note: The firm is renamed several times across the series as partners arrive and depart.

q: On the cover of the Beatles' 1969 album Abbey Road, what are the four members doing?
note: The London crossing was given protected landmark status in 2010.

q: What is the name of the Memphis mansion where Elvis Presley lived and is buried?
note: He bought it in 1957, when he was only 22 years old.

q: What is the title of Michael Jackson's 1982 album whose title track ends with a spoken passage by horror star Vincent Price?
note: Quincy Jones produced it, and its videos helped break the color barrier on early MTV.

q: Which Queen song from 1975 opens with the line 'Is this the real life? Is this just fantasy?'
note: It runs close to six minutes, which radio programmers insisted was far too long for a single.

q: Which band's 1991 single 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' pushed grunge into the mainstream?
note: Kurt Cobain took the title from a friend's graffiti, not realizing it named a brand of deodorant.

q: Which Swedish group won the 1974 Eurovision Song Contest with the song 'Waterloo'?
note: The name is an acronym built from the four members' first names.

q: Which 1973 Pink Floyd album has a prism splitting white light into a rainbow on its cover?
a: The Dark Side of the Moon
note: The sleeve was designed by the art studio Hipgnosis and carries almost no text at all.

q: Which American songwriter was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016?
note: He took weeks to acknowledge the prize and then skipped the ceremony altogether.

q: Which singer turned Otis Redding's song 'Respect' into a 1967 anthem?
note: Her version added the spelled-out chorus and the 'sock it to me' backing vocals sung by her sisters.

q: Which Buggles song was the first music video played on MTV in 1981?
note: MTV launched on August 1, 1981, and at first reached only a slice of New Jersey cable subscribers.

q: Whitney Houston's 1992 recording of 'I Will Always Love You' was written by which country singer?
note: Parton took her own version to number one on the country chart back in 1974.

q: Which band recorded the 1977 album Rumours while its couples were breaking up?
note: Two romances inside the band collapsed during the sessions, and the fallout became the songs.

q: What was the title of the Sugarhill Gang's 1979 single that first carried hip-hop onto mainstream radio?
note: Its backing track lifts the groove from Chic's disco hit 'Good Times.'

q: What was the name of the 1985 charity concert staged simultaneously at Wembley Stadium and Philadelphia's JFK Stadium?
note: Bob Geldof organized it to raise money for famine relief in Ethiopia.

q: Which musician starred in and wrote the songs for the 1984 film Purple Rain?
note: He won an Academy Award for the film's music.

q: Taylor Swift's 2014 album 1989 takes its title from what?
note: The record marked her deliberate move from country music to pop.

q: Under what name was the singer Elton John born?
note: He borrowed the 'John' from Long John Baldry, a singer he played alongside in his early years.

q: The 1969 Woodstock music festival was held on a dairy farm in which US state?
note: It took place on Max Yasgur's land near Bethel, not in the town of Woodstock at all.

q: Which Detroit record label, founded by Berry Gordy in 1959, launched the Supremes and the Temptations?
note: Its modest headquarters carried a sign reading Hitsville U.S.A.

q: What was the name of the flame-haired alien rock star alter ego David Bowie adopted for his 1972 album?
note: Bowie killed the character off from the stage in 1973, blindsiding both his fans and his own band.

q: Which actor played Indiana Jones in the 1981 film Raiders of the Lost Ark?
note: Tom Selleck was the first choice but was tied up filming the television series Magnum, P.I.

q: Which actor played the hotshot pilot Maverick in the 1986 film Top Gun?
note: The US Navy reported a surge of interest from would-be pilots after the film opened.

q: Which bodybuilder turned actor delivered the line 'I'll be back' in the 1984 film The Terminator?
note: He was elected governor of California nearly twenty years later, in 2003.

q: Which actress starred opposite Richard Gere in the 1990 romantic comedy Pretty Woman?
note: The script began life as a far darker drama before it was rewritten as a fairy tale.

q: Which Scottish actor was the first to play James Bond on screen, in the 1962 film Dr. No?
note: Author Ian Fleming thought him wrong for the part at first and only came round after seeing the film.

q: Which silent film star created the bowler-hatted, cane-twirling character known as the Little Tramp?
note: He helped found the studio United Artists in 1919 so that he could control his own films.

q: Which actor played the rebellious patient Randle McMurphy in the 1975 film One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest?
note: It brought him the first of his three acting Oscars.

q: Which actor improvised the line 'You talkin' to me?' as Travis Bickle in the 1976 film Taxi Driver?
note: The screenplay said only that Bickle talks to himself in the mirror.

q: Which actor both directed and starred in the 1992 western Unforgiven?
note: He held on to the script for years, waiting until he was old enough to play the worn-out gunfighter.

q: Which actress played Holly Golightly in the 1961 film Breakfast at Tiffany's?
note: She sang 'Moon River' herself, perched on a windowsill with a guitar.

q: Which actress's white dress billowed up over a subway grate in the 1955 film The Seven Year Itch?
note: The dress itself later sold at auction for millions of dollars.

q: Which actress became the first Black woman to win the Academy Award for Best Actress, for the 2001 film Monster's Ball?
note: Sidney Poitier was handed an honorary Oscar at the very same ceremony.

q: Which director made the 1979 Vietnam War epic Apocalypse Now?
note: The shoot in the Philippines dragged on for more than a year and nearly bankrupted him.

q: Which South Korean filmmaker won the Best Director Oscar for the 2019 film Parasite?
note: Parasite also became the first film not in English to win Best Picture.

q: Which comic actor won the Best Supporting Actor Oscar for playing a grieving therapist in the 1997 film Good Will Hunting?
note: Matt Damon and Ben Affleck won that same year's screenwriting Oscar for the film.

q: Which martial arts star died in 1973, a month before his film Enter the Dragon reached cinemas?
note: He was only 32, and the film turned him into a global icon after his death.

q: Which director slipped fleeting cameo appearances into most of his own films and never won a competitive Best Director Oscar?
note: He was nominated five times and finally given an honorary award in 1968.

q: Which actor became the first Black man to win the Best Actor Oscar, for the 1963 film Lilies of the Field?
note: He was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 1974.

q: Which actress won four Best Actress Oscars, the last of them for the 1981 film On Golden Pond?
note: She never once turned up at the ceremony to collect any of them.

q: Which actor starred in only three major films before dying in a 1955 car crash at the age of 24?
note: He became the first performer ever nominated for an acting Oscar after death.

q: In the Peanuts comic strip, what is the name of Charlie Brown's daydreaming beagle?
note: Charles Schulz drew the strip almost single-handedly for fifty years.

q: What is the name of the van the gang drives in the cartoon Scooby-Doo, which began in 1969?
note: The show's original title was Scooby-Doo, Where Are You!

q: In the 1994 animated film The Lion King, what is the name of Simba's father?
note: James Earl Jones, the voice of Darth Vader, supplied the voice.

q: Which chess piece moves in an L shape?
note: It is the only piece allowed to jump over the pieces in its way.

q: In Nintendo's Super Mario games, what job do the brothers Mario and Luigi have?
note: Mario is said to be named after the landlord of Nintendo's American warehouse.

q: What is the name of Superman's destroyed home planet?
note: He first appeared in Action Comics No. 1 in 1938.

q: Which 1995 Pixar release was the first feature film animated entirely on computers?
note: Pixar had spent its early years selling computer hardware before it turned to making films.

q: Which 1937 film was Walt Disney's first full-length animated feature?
a: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
note: Hollywood nicknamed the project 'Disney's Folly' right up until it became a hit.

q: In the American edition of Monopoly, which is the most expensive property square on the board?
note: The British edition puts Mayfair in the same corner of the board.

q: How many ghosts chase the player in the 1980 arcade game Pac-Man?
note: They are named Blinky, Pinky, Inky and Clyde.

q: The Rubik's Cube was invented in 1974 by Ernő Rubik, a teacher from which country?
note: Rubik taught architecture and built the cube to explain three-dimensional geometry to his students.

q: In Marvel comics, what is the name of the teenager who becomes Spider-Man after a radioactive spider bite in 1962?
note: Stan Lee and Steve Ditko created him for the final issue of a title that was already being canceled.

q: The board game Trivial Pursuit was created in 1979 by two newspapermen from which country?
note: Chris Haney and Scott Abbott dreamed it up in Montreal after finding pieces missing from their Scrabble set.

q: Which puppeteer created the Muppets and performed Kermit the Frog himself?
note: He used his own hand and voice for Kermit from the 1950s until his death in 1990.

q: The puzzle game Tetris was created in 1984 by a programmer working in which country?
note: Alexey Pajitnov saw almost no money from it for years, because the Soviet state held the rights.

q: In the Marvel comics and films, what fictional metal is Captain America’s shield made from?
note: In the stories it absorbs kinetic energy, which is why the shield can take a hit without transmitting the force.

q: Which 1960 cartoon was the first animated series to air in American prime time?
note: Its bickering couples were modeled closely on the live-action sitcom The Honeymooners.

q: Which 2001 Hayao Miyazaki film became the first Japanese animated feature to win an Academy Award?
note: Miyazaki stayed away from the ceremony in protest at the war in Iraq.

q: Which Belgian comic-strip reporter, created in 1929, travels the world with his small white dog Snowy?
note: His creator, Hergé, drew his adventures for more than fifty years.

q: In which 1978 arcade game do players shoot at rows of aliens marching steadily down the screen?
note: Made by Taito in Japan, it helped launch the golden age of the video arcade.
